newsitem.title: UK: TransCo to be sole dividend source for BG.
newsitem.headline: TransCo to be sole dividend source for BG.

text.p: TransCo, the gas transport operation of British Gas, will be the sole dividend source for BG Plc, which will be one of the two companies formed through British Gas' planned demerger, the company said.
BG's other assets besides TransCo include the exploration and production and international downstream operations.

But chief executive designate David Varney said these would be self-financing. "The board's intended policy is that...TransCo's current cost profit after servicing its regulatory capital and after taxatation, should be dedicated to paying BG's dividend," Varney told a news conference.

TransCo is currently awaiting the outcome of an investigation by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC), which is vetting price regime proposals put forward by industry regulator Ofgas and rejected by British Gas.
As long as the inquiry lasts it was impossible to outline BG's dividend policy, Varney said.

British Gas said earlier that it planned to maintain its full 1996 dividend at 14.5 pence. Chairman Richard Giordano said the company's board had decided it would not be wise to change the pay-out pending the MMC investigation.
But in a statement British Gas added: "This payment should not be taken as a guide to likely future levels of dividend which are expected to be materially lower."
Analysts had said earlier that British Gas' dividend would have to be cut by some 10 percent if the Ofgas price proposals were implemented.
The split-up of British Gas will also involve the formation of Centrica, which will house the gas trading business.
Centrica is not expected to pay dividends in the immediate future, said chief executive designate Roy Gardner.
"There are a number of uncertainties which must be clarified before the directors of the company will be able to assess the approriate level of dividend in the medium term," he told journalists.
The uncertainties include progress on renegotiating take-or-pay contracts with gas producers and the loss of market share during the gradual liberalisation of the domestic gas market.
